title: Scientific Imaging Foundations
description: Build a repeatable method for inspecting and interpreting medical images.

lessons.title: Orienting to Cross-sectional Imaging
lessons.description: Recognize orientation and establish a consistent inspection sequence.

content.heading: Use a repeatable search pattern
content.body: A systematic review reduces missed findings and supports defensible interpretation.

lessons.title: CT Windowing
lessons.description: Choose display windows that reveal the anatomy under investigation.

content.alt: Diagram showing narrow and wide CT display windows
content.caption: Window width controls contrast; center selects the displayed attenuation range.

lessons.title: Interpreting Thoracic CT
lessons.description: Apply an inspection sequence and connect appearance to tissue properties.

content.heading: Inspect before interpreting
content.body: First establish image quality, orientation and the current display window.
content.keyTakeaway: Describe the evidence before naming the pattern.

content.caption: Use bilateral comparison as part of the search pattern.

content.prompt: Which action should come before interpreting a subtle lung opacity?

options.label: Confirm the display window and image quality

content.explanation: Display settings and technical quality can materially change apparent findings.

content.prompt: Explore the stack and compare lung and mediastinal windows.

lessons.title: Thoracic Case Practice
lessons.description: Apply the inspection sequence to a short clinical case.

nodes.body: A 67-year-old with fever and increasing oxygen requirement has a new focal opacity on a portable chest image. You are asked to review the available thoracic imaging.

asset.alt: Simplified axial thorax diagram showing bilateral lungs and mediastinum
asset.caption: Use a systematic bilateral comparison before interpreting a focal finding.

choices.label: Verify orientation, image quality and display settings
choices.consequence: You establish that the study is technically adequate and avoid mistaking display artifacts for pathology.
choices.quality: Best: establishes whether the evidence is interpretable.

choices.label: Name the most likely diagnosis immediately
choices.consequence: The early label narrows attention before the technical quality has been checked.
choices.quality: Premature: interpretation should follow technical review.

nodes.body: The study is correctly oriented and the lung window is appropriate. The focal opacity persists on adjacent slices.
A colleague asks whether the opacity could be positional. Returning to the technical review confirms the finding persists on adjacent slices.

nodes.prompt: How should you characterize the finding?

choices.label: Compare both lungs and describe distribution before assigning a cause
choices.consequence: The comparison confirms a unilateral dependent opacity without a similar contralateral finding.

choices.label: Base the interpretation on the most striking slice
choices.consequence: The apparent severity changes across nearby slices, making the single-slice impression unreliable.
choices.quality: Limited: adjacent anatomy is needed to establish the pattern.

nodes.body: The opacity is confirmed across slices. The patient has fever, productive cough and rising inflammatory markers.

nodes.prompt: What is the most defensible communication?

choices.label: Report the observed pattern, likely infectious cause and relevant uncertainty
choices.consequence: The care team receives a clear finding linked to the clinical context without overstating certainty.
choices.quality: Best: evidence, interpretation and uncertainty remain distinct.

choices.label: State a definitive diagnosis without qualification
choices.consequence: The report communicates more certainty than the imaging evidence supports.
choices.quality: Overconfident: imaging findings should be integrated with clinical evidence.

nodes.title: A defensible thoracic interpretation
nodes.body: The team treats a probable focal infection while monitoring the clinical response and preserving alternative explanations.
nodes.result: A repeatable sequence—technical review, pattern description and clinical correlation—produced an actionable interpretation.

lessons.title: Imaging Lab
lessons.description: Manipulate a curated CT stack and record a measurement.

content.prompt: Follow a short inspection sequence to locate the tracheal air column.

steps.instruction: Navigate to slices 78–86 and find the central air-filled trachea.
Inspect adjacent slices, then confirm that the structure is continuous.

checkpoint.prompt: Which structure is the central dark oval anterior to the oesophagus?
checkpoint.explanation: Air in the trachea appears dark and remains continuous through adjacent superior thoracic slices.

content.prompt: Select the tracheal air column on a representative slice.

region.label: Tracheal air column
region.description: Central air-filled lumen anterior to the oesophagus.

content.explanation: The tracheal air column is the central dark oval on these superior thoracic slices.
content.sliceFeedback: Navigate to the superior thorax around slices 78–86.
content.locationFeedback: Look for the central dark oval just anterior to the oesophagus.

content.prompt: Measure the transverse inner diameter of the tracheal air column.
content.explanation: The tracheal air column is the central dark oval anterior to the oesophagus. The reference inner diameter is 17.6 mm on slice 81.
